title: Robust recommendation commit protocol and event listener for Optimize automation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Ship a reliable API + event listener that lets Optimize automatically propose, stage, and safely commit batching/caching recommendations with automatic rollback on failure. This ticket focuses on the control-plane surface (endpoints + event contract) and SDK helpers needed for idempotent, observable apply operations.
design_summary: We will implement a prepare/confirm handshake (prepare returns an apply_token and preview diff; confirm completes the change). Each apply is guarded by an Idempotency-Key header and an apply_token TTL. The control plane will emit deterministic events to a webhook endpoint (or internal event bus) for audit, observability, and downstream orchestration. SDK will provide helpers to: (1) create a dry-run, (2) call prepare, (3) wait for preflight checks, (4) confirm or cancel. The service will maintain an apply ledger to dedupe requests and store outcome metadata for retries and rollbacks.
webhook_payload_examples:
We will send compact, signed webhook events to registered listeners. Examples below are shown as JSON text for readability (actual payloads are HMAC-signed):

Event: optimize.apply.prepared
{
  "event_type": "optimize.apply.prepared",
  "apply_token": "token-abc",
  "recommendation_id": "rec-7721",
  "target": "proj:route-alpha",
  "preview_url": "https://console/...",
  "est_cost_savings": 120.5,
  "metadata": { "created_by": "optimize-runner" }
}

Event: optimize.apply.completed
{
  "event_type": "optimize.apply.completed",
  "change_id": "chg-20250303-01",
  "status": "applied",
  "duration_ms": 512,
  "diff_url": "https://console/...",
  "audit": { "actor": "system:optimize" }
}

Event: optimize.apply.failed
{
  "event_type": "optimize.apply.failed",
  "change_id": "chg-20250303-01",
  "status": "failed",
  "reason": "quota_exceeded",
  "rollback_initiated": true
}
acceptance_criteria: Prepare endpoint accepts recommendation payloads and returns apply_token + preview within SLAs (p95 < 300ms for small diffs).
Confirm endpoint is idempotent: repeated confirm with same Idempotency-Key returns same result and does not duplicate changes.
Server persists apply ledger entries with status transitions (prepared -> confirming -> applied|failed -> rolled_back) for audit and retries.
Webhook events delivered with retries and signature header; sample listener in SDK consumes events and maps them to change state.
Client SDK exposes simple flow helpers (dryRun(), prepare(), confirm(), cancel()) and surface clear error types (Retryable vs Fatal).
Automatic rollback triggers on post-apply health checks failure (console health probe) and emits optimize.apply.failed + optimize.rollback.started events.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag gate behind optimize.autoupdate toggle per org. 2) Internal canary: enable for engineering orgs (5%) for 48 hours. 3) Monitor change failures and webhook delivery errors on dashboard. 4) Gradual ramp to 100% over two weeks with automatic rollback of feature flag if failure rate > 1% of applies.
test_plan: Unit tests for idempotency ledger, e2e tests covering prepare->confirm->status, load test for p95 prepare latency, chaos tests that kill config-apply workers to validate rollback behavior, and integration test for webhook signature verification and replay handling. Create test harness that simulates duplicate Idempotency-Key and mutated payload to assert 409 and correct dedupe behavior.
notes: Design choice: prefer prepare/confirm handshake instead of direct mutate-on-prepare to provide operator preview and human-in-the-loop control for enterprise tenants.
Security: webhooks must include x-redwood-signature and listeners should validate clock skew. Rotate webhook signing keys via KMS integration; see security checklist.
Operational: add Prometheus metrics for idempotency conflicts, apply_token expirations, webhook delivery latency and webhook 5xx rate.
